prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Lange deutsche Komposita (language de).
Grid: 3 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Begriff" · longest unbreakable word 546px · one-line width 546px
  col 2: header "Kurzform" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 101px
  col 3: header "Erklärung" · longest unbreakable word 186px · one-line width 1091px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 720px. You MAY choose a total wider than 719px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
An earlier design attempt for this table was rejected by independent reviewers. Their comments: another layout was rated good: All three columns fit in view, the short forms stay intact, and the explanations have a readable measure. The two longest terms break within words, but most row labels remain intact. | your previous preferred design was rated poor: The terms and short forms stay intact, but the explanation column begins at the edge of the viewport, so reading the table requires substantial horizontal scrolling. | another layout was rated good: The table fits in view and gives the explanations slightly more room. Two long terms split within words, and Kfz-Haftpflicht wraps across two lines. | another layout was rated bad: The long terms stay intact, but almost the entire explanation column lies beyond the viewport. The narrow explanation column also produces tall rows, and Kfz-Haftpflicht wraps. | another layout was rated poor: Equal column widths waste space on the mostly short abbreviations. Nearly every term breaks awkwardly, while the narrow explanations make the table tall. | another layout was rated acceptable: The short forms stay intact and the explanations have comfortable space, but the narrow first column splits nearly every row label, making the terms harder to scan.
another layout was rated good: The table fits the viewport and gives the terms and explanations useful space. Two long terms split within words, and Kfz-Haftpflicht wraps. | another layout was rated poor: The terms stay intact, but the explanation column begins at the viewport edge and requires horizontal scrolling. Its narrow measure also makes the rows tall. | another layout was rated good: The table fits the viewport, keeps the short forms intact, and balances the terms against readable explanations. Two long terms still split within words. | another layout was rated acceptable: The explanations have comfortable space and the table fits, but nearly every row label breaks within a word, making the terms harder to scan. | your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: Terms and short forms stay intact, but almost all explanations lie beyond the viewport, so readers must scroll to connect them with their terms. | another layout was rated poor: The wide short-form column wastes space while row labels split repeatedly and explanations wrap into narrow, tall blocks.

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Die Tabelle ordnet lange deutsche Komposita ihren Kurzformen und Erklärungen zu.","reading":"Lesende suchen einen Begriff oder eine Kurzform und lesen dann die Erklärung in derselben Zeile; alle drei Spalten sollten dafür möglichst gleichzeitig sichtbar sein.","groups":["Begriff und Kurzform bezeichnen denselben Gegenstand und sollten leicht zeilenweise zuzuordnen sein.","Die Erklärung ergänzt beide Bezeichnungen und braucht genügend Breite für zusammenhängenden Fließtext."],"keep_intact":["Kurzformen möglichst vollständig, insbesondere Kfz-Haftpflicht.","Begriffe möglichst als erkennbare Zeilenkennungen; bei den längsten Komposita sind Wortumbrüche innerhalb des verfügbaren Platzes unvermeidbar."],"may_wrap":["Erklärungen können an Wortgrenzen über mehrere Zeilen laufen.","Die längsten Begriffe dürfen innerhalb des Wortes umbrechen; diese Zeilenhöhe kann zugleich Umbrüche der Erklärung aufnehmen."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[360,122,237],"idea":"Ausgewogene Ansicht: Begriffe und Erklärungen erhalten nutzbare Breiten, während auch die längste Kurzform in einer Zeile bleibt."},{"name":"B","widths":[310,122,287],"idea":"Erklärungsbetonte Ansicht: Mehr Platz für den Fließtext verkürzt dessen Zeilenblöcke, verlangt aber häufigere Umbrüche in den Begriffen."},{"name":"C","widths":[400,105,214],"idea":"Begriffsbetonte Ansicht: Die breitere erste Spalte erleichtert das Scannen der Zeilenkennungen, während Kfz-Haftpflicht und die Erklärungen mehr umbrechen."}]}
